name: Poseidon
what_it_is: Poseidon is an SDN-based network situational awareness tool that uses Software Defined Networking and machine learning to automatically capture network traffic via port mirroring, extract IP header features, and classify devices on the network. It integrates tightly with the FAUCET SDN controller to dynamically reconfigure mirroring and apply ACLs based on ML-derived device roles.
components: poseidon (core orchestrator, exposes Prometheus metrics on :9304)
network_tap (traffic capture orchestrator, manages ncapture containers)
workers (ML classification workers, spawns Docker containers per capture job)
rabbit / RabbitMQ (message broker for FAUCET events and internal coordination)
rabbitmq_adapter / event-adapter-rabbitmq (bridges FAUCET event socket to RabbitMQ)
faucetconfrpc (gRPC server for remote FAUCET config management, :59999)
faucet_certstrap (one-shot TLS cert generator for faucetconfrpc)
NetworkML (external ML classifier, referenced via network-tools)
ncapture (per-host pcap capture sidecar, from IQTLabs/network-tools)
protocols: RabbitMQ AMQP (FAUCET.Event messages, routing key FAUCET.Event)
gRPC / faucetconfrpc (remote FAUCET YAML config updates, port 59999)
Prometheus exposition format (metrics scrape on port 9304)
PCAP / libpcap (raw traffic capture via ncapture)
measurement: poseidon_last_rabbitmq_routing_key_time gauge tracks last FAUCET.Event received timestamp
pcap files accumulated in /opt/poseidon_files (configurable via POSEIDON_PREFIX)
Per-host traffic captures written as trace_<hash>_<timestamp>.pcap
configuration: Primary config: /opt/poseidon/poseidon.config (INI format, sections: Poseidon, Faucet, VOLOS, PIPETTE)
collector_nic: NIC interface name receiving mirrored traffic (must be up before Poseidon starts)
controller_mirror_ports: JSON dict mapping switch name to mirror port number
controller_proxy_mirror_ports: JSON dict for switches without dedicated mirror ports
faucetconfrpc_address: gRPC endpoint for FAUCET config (default faucetconfrpc:59999)
tunnel_vlan / tunnel_name: VLAN ID and ACL name for FAUCET remote mirroring tunnels
FAUCET_EVENT_SOCK=1 and FAUCET_CONFIG_STAT_RELOAD=1 must be set on the FAUCET container
automated_acls: whether Poseidon automatically applies ACL rules (default False)
ignore_vlans, ignore_ports, trunk_ports: JSON dicts/lists for exclusions
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection framework; no chaos or failure simulation features documented
Troubleshooting relies on inspecting RabbitMQ adapter status and pcap accumulation manually
modes: poseidon start: full mode — Poseidon manages and starts FAUCET alongside itself
poseidon start --standalone: standalone mode — connects to a separately-managed FAUCET instance
Faucet stacking mode: single Poseidon mirror port on root switch with loopback plugs on non-root switches; Poseidon auto-detects and uses FAUCET tunneling
Remote FAUCET mode: faucetconfrpc and rabbitmq_adapter run on Faucet host, Poseidon on separate host
constraints: Requires a physical or virtual FAUCET SDN controller running OpenFlow 1.3; not compatible with arbitrary SDN controllers
collector_nic interface must be up and connected to the switch mirror port BEFORE Poseidon starts — it will not detect hosts if the interface is down at startup
Only one collector_nic supported per Poseidon instance; to mirror multiple switches centrally, FAUCET stacking must be used
Requires ~10 GB free disk space for pcap storage in /opt/poseidon_files
Docker overlay network required (docker-compose uses driver: overlay) — typically needs Docker Swarm mode or equivalent
Installation on macOS is possible but not officially supported
Installation from .deb package no longer supported; must use the poseidon shell script
faucetconfrpc TLS certificates must be provisioned (via faucet_certstrap) before poseidon container becomes healthy
docker_services: network_tap (iqtlabs/network_tap:v0.11.33, mounts docker.sock and poseidon_files volume)
poseidon (iqtlabs/poseidon, port 9304 Prometheus, mounts config and faucetconfrpc certs)
workers (iqtlabs/poseidon-workers, mounts docker.sock, spawns ML worker containers)
notable_absences: No built-in FAUCET simulator or OpenFlow software switch (e.g., Open vSwitch) in docker-compose — a real or external FAUCET+switch setup is required
No included ML model training pipeline — NetworkML models must be pre-trained externally
No built-in network traffic replay or pcap injection mechanism for testing without live traffic
No HTTPS/TLS on the poseidon_api REST endpoint by default
No native support for non-FAUCET SDN controllers (e.g., ONOS, OpenDaylight)
